title: Frijol colado with butter, onion and Parmesan
description: Finely pureed black beans simmer with softened onion and butter into a smooth, spoonable side. A little grated Parmesan around the plate adds a salty finish.

ingredients.name: drained cooked black beans
ingredients.substitution: Use the same drained weight of fully cooked pinto beans for a lighter-colored adaptation.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a firm dairy-free butter alternative; flavor changes. Soft low-fat spreads contain more water.

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of white or yellow onion. Shallots give a milder, sweeter result.

ingredients.name: finely grated Parmesan
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of finely grated aged hard cheese; saltiness differs.

Finely chop {{item-3}}. Melt {{item-2|0.8}} in a saucepan over medium-low heat; cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the bean puree and simmer gently for 5–8 minutes, stirring often, until hot and spoonable. If it becomes stiff, stir in a small splash of water.
Spoon onto a warm plate. Put {{item-2|0.2}} on top to melt, and sprinkle {{item-4}} around the edge. Serve warm.

title: Frijoles negros volteados with plantain and cheese
description: Smooth black beans are slowly fried until thick enough to turn onto a plate as a soft oval mound. Golden ripe plantain and fresh cheese balance the rich, earthy beans.

ingredients.name: drained cooked black beans
ingredients.substitution: Use the same drained weight of fully cooked canned black beans. Red beans change the flavor and color; do not use raw dried beans.

ingredients.name: bean cooking liquid
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of water if bean liquid is unavailable.

ingredients.name: lard
ingredients.substitution: Use 30 ml canola oil for a version without lard; the cheese still contains dairy.

ingredients.name: peeled ripe plantain
ingredients.substitution: Use yellow plantain with black patches. Dessert bananas soften much faster and are not a direct replacement.

ingredients.name: canola oil
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of sunflower or canola oil.

ingredients.name: pasteurized queso fresco
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of paneer or a firm mild fresh cheese; texture and saltiness differ.

steps: Blend {{item-0}} with {{item-1}} until smooth, scraping down the blender as needed.

Melt {{item-2}} in a 24 cm nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the bean puree carefully and stir frequently for 15–25 minutes until it pulls away from the pan and holds a soft mound. Reduce heat if it spatters or sticks.

Meanwhile, cut {{item-3}} into diagonal slices about 1 cm thick. Heat {{item-4}} in a second skillet over medium heat and fry the plantain in a single layer for 3–4 minutes per side, until golden and tender. Work in batches if needed.
Use a spatula to fold the thick beans into an oval; gently roll onto a plate, or spoon into a mound if it does not turn cleanly. Slice {{item-5}} and serve alongside the fried plantain.
notes: Four portions. Total time and yield are estimates; adjust pans and cook in batches for larger yields. title: Gallina Caprichosa (Capricious Chicken)
description: Prepared with chicken, chicken breast, and chicken liver.
steps: After plucking and cleaning the chicken well, remove the skin with great care so it does not break

Place in a serving dish covering it with water, bay leaves, thyme, a garlic head, a bunch of leeks and onion

steps: While the leg is still very hot (just removed), prick it with a fork and flatten it very well with a mallet
Mix 1 ounce of saltpeter with 1 pound of salt and rub the leg very hard with this mixture

The next day, rub it with the same salt and continue rubbing it daily with the same salt for twenty days

Remove that water and place it back on the fire with 1 bottle of red wine and water until the leg is covered
Add about 6 bay leaves, sprigs of thyme, 1 bunch of parsley, 1 bunch of leeks, and 1 ounce of Castilian pepper

steps: Prepare a two-month-old piglet and feed it sweetened milk with bread for eight days.

Make a fried mixture with plenty of onion and tomato; add the meat, vegetables, about two ounces of pitted raisins, one ounce of almonds, olives, capers, pitted prunes, a little vinegar and sugar to taste, a little clove powder, pepper and cinnamon, and one small glass of sherry wine.

When well cooked, after about two hours, decorate with lettuce and serve with Russian salad
